properties.description:
The retirement rule of req:the-mcp-server-keeps-working-as-is-and-door-improvements-are-additive-or-opt-in as amended on @ajs's word 2026-10-13: "never removed" becomes "never removed WITHOUT A RELEASE OF NOTICE"; anything a client can call or read is retired in two releases, a DEPRECATING release in which it still works, says it is going and the changelog carries a "What to do" line, then the NEXT release removes it; and "the check that the served surface only grows becomes a check that it shrinks only through a deprecating release."

As built 2026-10-14 (#751). ONE PLACE: deprecation::REGISTRY (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/deprecation.rs), empty until the first real deprecation. Each entry gives the item (a tool, a tool argument, a reply field at a path, a node type, an edge type or a node property), the version that deprecates it, what to do instead in one sentence, and the dec: that retires it. THE MARK: a deprecated tool's or argument's description opens with "DEPRECATED in <version>, removed in the next release: <what to do>"; a deprecated reply field is named with the mark in its tool's description; describe_schema puts `deprecated` on a node type, property or edge type and its full answer lists every entry under `deprecations`. THE NOTICE: a call that uses a deprecated item (calls the tool, passes the argument, names or reads back the type, writes or reads the property, gets the reply field) gets a `deprecation_notice` field in its structured reply, or one more text block on a reply with no structured half. A field because it is additive and both client populations read it: content_policy builds a content-only client's text block from the structured reply. THE TOOL STUB: a tool removed in the next release keeps its entry for that release and its old name is refused with what to do, in a session and at the --call door, as dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first requires. THE CHECK: tests/the_mcp_surface_only_grows.rs (name kept) records the release's vocabulary and deprecations from its own describe_schema at a bless; a removal passes only when the record marks it deprecated, a deprecated item still served passes, and a removed tool must still answer its old name. THE CHANGELOG: every entry is named under ### Deprecated with a What to do line, in a changelog.d fragment until its release is cut and then in that release's CHANGELOG.md section (tests/every_deprecation_is_announced_in_the_changelog.rs). With the registry empty nothing a client sees changes: the 197 toolsnaps match and every reply is unchanged. The release-cut step is cap:a-cuts-release-notes-say-what-is-going-and-what-has-gone. Who tells Alex, and how, is Anthony's open decision (D3); nothing here assumes an answer.
properties.name: A served item is removed only after a release that announced it: one registry declares each deprecation, the surface marks it, a call that uses it is told, and the surface check lets the next release remove it
